note: Recipes for ORIGINAL SAT-style questions (The 1600 Project). Each blueprint: technique, how to build it, the mistake behind each wrong answer, and what makes it harder. Questions are written from these only, never from College Board items.

blueprints.title: Line from two points → intercept
blueprints.technique: slope = Δy/Δx, then plug in a point for b.
blueprints.build: Two points; integer slope at easy, fraction slope at hard.
blueprints.harder: negative coordinates; ask for the x-intercept; put the points in a context.

blueprints.title: Perpendicular line through a point
blueprints.technique: From Ax + By = C, slope = −A/B; flip it and switch the sign; point-slope form.
blueprints.build: A, B, point (x1, y1). Make x1 a multiple of A·B so all four lines have integer intercepts.
blueprints.harder: slope-intercept given at easy; standard form at medium; standard form with negative B at hard. All four choices should pass through the point, so plugging in can't eliminate any.

blueprints.title: Table → f(x), input vs. output
blueprints.technique: slope = Δf/Δx where x steps by more than 1; f(k) gives an output, f(a) = v asks for an input.
blueprints.build: x-step 2–5, slope, intercept.
wrong: answered f(k) when asked for a, or the reverse
blueprints.harder: table doesn't start at x = 0; grid-in.

skills: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
blueprints.title: Inequality with whole-number rounding
blueprints.technique: "at most" → ≤; isolate; the story forces the rounding direction.
blueprints.build: Capacity, fixed amount, per-unit amount, with a non-integer quotient whose decimal is ≥ .5, so normal rounding gives the trap.
blueprints.harder: "at least" version (round up); two kinds of units.

skills: Systems of two linear equations in two variables
blueprints.title: Count-and-total system
blueprints.technique: One equation per fact (count, total value); solve; answer the variable asked.
blueprints.build: Total count, two unit prices, positive-integer solution.
wrong: a value from adding the prices
blueprints.harder: "which system models…"; ask for a combination like x + 2y; decimal prices.

blueprints.title: Threshold-cost model
blueprints.technique: Only units past the threshold cost extra: base + rate(t − threshold). Test a value.
blueprints.build: Base fee, included units, overage rate.
blueprints.harder: ask for the cost at a specific t; included units given in hours vs. minutes.

skills: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
blueprints.title: Point in a system of inequalities
blueprints.technique: Test each point in both inequalities; strict inequalities exclude the boundary.
blueprints.build: Two lines, four candidate points.
wrong: lies exactly on a strict (<, >) boundary
blueprints.harder: one inequality given in standard form; a one-variable inequality needing the sign flip.

blueprints.title: Solve for the expression
blueprints.technique: The expression asked for is a multiple of the given one; scale, don't solve.
blueprints.build: Given px + qy = r, asked for (p/k)x + (q/k)y or kpx + kqy. One-variable versions (given 3x − 5 = 13, find 6x − 10) count as 'Linear equations in one variable'.
blueprints.harder: two variables (can't be solved otherwise) at medium–hard; a negative scale factor.

blueprints.title: Difference of squares shortcut
blueprints.technique: x² − y² = (x + y)(x − y); divide by the given factor.
blueprints.build: x, y integers; give x² − y² and x + y.
wrong: x or y instead of x − y
blueprints.harder: ask for x or y (add the two factor equations); disguise it, e.g. 4a² − 9b².

blueprints.title: Match coefficients for all x
blueprints.technique: Expand; match constants first, then the x-terms. Desmos: regress y₁ ~ unknown form.
blueprints.build: (px + a)(x − q) = px² + bx + c, or a(x + h)² + b = expanded form.
wrong: answering a when asked for b
dropping the 2ab term of a square
blueprints.harder: two unknowns inside different factors at hard.

blueprints.title: Quadratic features: zeros, vertex, min/max
blueprints.technique: Factor or read the vertex; the min VALUE is the y-coordinate, WHERE it occurs is x.
blueprints.build: x² + bx + c with integer zeros; vertex may be a half-integer.
wrong: x-coordinate when asked for the minimum value (or the reverse)
a zero with the wrong sign
blueprints.harder: vertex form vs. standard form; leading coefficient ≠ 1.

skills: Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables
blueprints.title: Line meets parabola: number of solutions / find k
blueprints.technique: Set equal, move to one side, use the discriminant (0 = tangent, one solution).
blueprints.build: Parabola and line chosen so the difference is a perfect square for the tangent case.
wrong: k from forgetting to move the line's constant
blueprints.harder: count solutions at medium; solve for k at hard.

blueprints.title: Evaluate vs. solve; transformations
blueprints.technique: f(2) means evaluate, f(x) = 2 means solve; f(x + h) moves LEFT h; + k moves up.
blueprints.build: f in vertex form, g(x) = f(x + h) + k.
wrong: vertex of f instead of g
blueprints.harder: composition f(g(a)); a reflection.

blueprints.title: Exponential growth/decay model
blueprints.technique: a(1 ± r)^t; a 15% decrease is ×0.85.
blueprints.build: Initial value, rate, time; pick values with exact results.
wrong: one period too many or too few
blueprints.harder: "which model fits" with four forms; when does it fall below a target.

skills: One-variable data: distributions and measures of center and spread
blueprints.title: Mean after adding or removing a value
blueprints.technique: Think in sums: mean × count = sum; adjust the sum; divide by the NEW count.
blueprints.build: Count, mean, removed/added value; clean new mean.
wrong: subtracted the value from the mean
blueprints.harder: two values removed; find the removed value from both means.

blueprints.title: Two-way table conditional probability
blueprints.technique: The group after "given" or "of the" picks the denominator.
blueprints.build: 2×2 table with totals, as a Markdown table.
wrong: the reversed condition (row total vs. column total)
blueprints.harder: 3×2 table; ask for a percent.

blueprints.title: Line of best fit: slope, intercept, predicted vs. actual
blueprints.technique: m = predicted change in y for each 1-unit change in x; b = predicted y when x = 0; residual = actual − predicted; constant differences → linear, constant ratios → exponential.
blueprints.build: A model y = mx + b in a context, plus one actual data point; or a small table of values. No scatterplot images.
wrong: slope read as the change in x per unit of y
the intercept described as a rate
above and below the prediction swapped
treating the predicted value as exact
claiming one variable causes the other
blueprints.harder: choose the interpretation sentence; pick linear vs. exponential from a table.

skills: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error
Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
blueprints.title: Sampling, margin of error and study design
blueprints.technique: A result applies only to the population that was randomly sampled; estimate ± margin gives a plausible range, not an exact value; bigger sample → smaller margin; only random assignment supports cause and effect.
blueprints.build: A study description: who was sampled, how, the result and the margin. Margin and range questions are 'Inference from sample statistics…'; causation and generalization questions are 'Evaluating statistical claims…'.
wrong: generalizes to a larger or different population
treats the estimate as the exact value
claims causation from an observational study
says a larger sample increases the margin
blueprints.harder: volunteer sample with random assignment (causation, but only for people like the volunteers); comparing two margins.

blueprints.title: Special right triangles
blueprints.technique: 30-60-90 is x, x√3, 2x (short leg opposite 30°); 45-45-90 is x, x, x√2.
blueprints.build: One known side and an angle, described in words (no figure).
wrong: treated the hypotenuse as the short leg (e.g. 10√3)
blueprints.harder: long leg given (divide by √3); embedded in a rectangle or equilateral triangle.

blueprints.title: Parallel lines and a transversal
blueprints.technique: Same-side interior angles add to 180°; alternate and corresponding angles are equal.
blueprints.build: Two angle expressions in x, described in words (no figure).
wrong: set them equal instead of supplementary
reported x instead of the angle
the other angle of the pair
blueprints.harder: a vertical-angle step added.

blueprints.title: Complementary sine and cosine
blueprints.technique: Opposite/adjacent from each angle; sin A = cos B when A + B = 90°.
blueprints.build: A Pythagorean triple (3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17, or multiples); triangle described in words.
wrong: the other leg over the hypotenuse
blueprints.harder: sides scaled; given sin x° = cos(ky + c)°, solve for y.

blueprints.title: Circle equation by completing the square
blueprints.technique: Move the constant, add (half the coefficient)² to both sides; r is the square root.
blueprints.build: Center (h, k), radius r; expand into general form.
wrong: forgot to add the squares to the right side
blueprints.harder: leading coefficient 2 (divide first); ask for diameter or area.

blueprints.title: Arc length and radians
blueprints.technique: arc = (θ/360)·2πr; radians = degrees × π/180.
blueprints.build: Radius, central angle that divides 360 nicely.
blueprints.harder: given arc length, find the angle; sector area version.

blueprints.title: Similar figures and solids
blueprints.technique: Lengths scale by k, areas by k², volumes by k³.
blueprints.build: Two corresponding lengths, one area or volume. Similar triangles are 'Lines, angles, and triangles'; areas and volumes of similar figures are 'Area and volume'.
wrong: scaled by k² for a volume
blueprints.harder: given the volume ratio, find the length ratio.

skills: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
blueprints.title: Proportions, rates and unit conversion
blueprints.technique: Keep the same units in the same position: (flour/sugar) = (flour/sugar). Convert by multiplying by fractions equal to 1 and cancelling units. Rate × time = amount; density × volume = mass.
blueprints.build: A ratio or rate, a target amount, and conversion factors that give an integer answer.
wrong: flipped one side of the proportion
converted area or volume with the plain length factor (1 ft² = 12 in²)
mixed minutes and hours in one rate
blueprints.harder: two conversions in a row; squared or cubed units; density.

blueprints.title: Percentages and multipliers
blueprints.technique: part = percent × whole; percent change = (new − old) / old; up r% is ×(1 + r), down r% is ×(1 − r); successive changes multiply; reverse a discount by dividing.
blueprints.build: An original value and rate(s) that give clean results.
wrong: took the percent of the sale price to undo a discount
divided by the new value in percent change
used the rate in place of what remains (×0.30 for 30% off)
blueprints.harder: chained changes; percent of a percent; working backward from a final amount.

skills: Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables
blueprints.title: Test the answer choices
blueprints.technique: When the choices are numbers and the question gives a function or equation, test all four. In Desmos, put them in a list, e.g. g([2,4,5,6]).
blueprints.build: An equation that's slow to solve by hand but fast to check, with exactly one choice that works.
wrong: a value that works in only one equation of a system
a value that gives the right output for a different function
an extraneous solution (from squaring or a rational equation)
blueprints.harder: radical or rational equations where one tempting choice is extraneous.

blueprints.title: Table regression → value or constant
blueprints.technique: Type the table into Desmos and run y₁ ~ mx₁ + b (or y₁ ~ a·b^{x₁}); read the constant or evaluate the model.
blueprints.build: A table (Markdown) of a linear or exponential function where x doesn't step by 1 or start at 0; ask for f(k), the intercept, or the growth factor. All values exact.
wrong: slope taken as Δy, ignoring the x-step
the first table row used as the intercept
the growth rate given in place of the factor (0.2 vs. 1.2)
the value at the wrong input
blueprints.harder: exponential with a twist like f(x) = a·b^{x/2}; a constant in a given form.

blueprints.title: Regression for constants in an identity ("for all x")
blueprints.technique: Graph the known side as y₁ over a list of x values, then regress onto the form with unknown constants, e.g. y₁ ~ (ax + b)(x − c).
blueprints.build: An identity with 2–3 unknown constants; ask for one of them or a combination.
wrong: a different constant than the one asked for
the sum given when the product is asked for (or the reverse)
blueprints.harder: a rational-expression form; ask for ab or a + c.

blueprints.title: List regression: constants from points
blueprints.technique: Put the given points into lists and regress the stated form (y₁ ~ a(x₁ − h)² + k, y₁ ~ a·b^{x₁}) to get every constant at once.
blueprints.build: A function with 2–3 unknown constants that passes through 2–3 given points.
wrong: f(0) given when a constant is asked for (or the reverse)
blueprints.harder: vertex form with an unknown h; exponential through two points that aren't at x = 0.

blueprints.title: Joining two complete sentences
blueprints.technique: Split Test. Join only with a period, a semicolon, comma + FANBOYS, or a colon when the second part explains the first.
blueprints.build: A passage with a blank at the join between two independent clauses.
blueprints.harder: long clauses with harmless inner commas; fake joiner placed mid-clause.

blueprints.title: Matching extra-information pairs
blueprints.technique: Removal test; close with the same mark that opened (comma/comma, dash/dash).
blueprints.build: A sentence with a nonessential element; the blank is at its close.
blueprints.harder: blank at the opening; a restrictive clause that needs no commas.

blueprints.title: Colon before a list or explanation
blueprints.technique: A complete sentence before the colon; a list or explanation after.
blueprints.build: A blank before a list or explanation.
blueprints.harder: an incomplete clause before the blank, so no punctuation is correct.

blueprints.title: Subject–verb agreement
blueprints.technique: Cross out the middle ("of…" phrases, anything between commas); match the verb to what's left. Each/every/the number of = singular; a number of/A and B = plural.
blueprints.build: A blank for the main verb, with a separated subject.
wrong: wrong tense in the right number
blueprints.harder: subject separated by a long prepositional phrase; an "along with" phrase.

blueprints.title: Pronoun agreement
blueprints.technique: One thing (including one company, team, committee) = it/its; more = they/their.
blueprints.build: A blank for a pronoun or possessive determiner.
blueprints.harder: the antecedent is two sentences back.

blueprints.title: Verb tense from the timeline
blueprints.technique: Clue words set the tense (in 1905 → past; since → present perfect; by the time → past perfect); with no clues, match the other verbs.
blueprints.build: A blank for a verb whose tense is fixed by the passage.
wrong: present perfect with a finished past date
blueprints.harder: no clue words in the sentence itself, only in the surrounding text.

blueprints.title: Apostrophes and possessives
blueprints.technique: its = belongs to it, it's = it is; -'s one owner, -s' many owners; plurals take no apostrophe.
blueprints.build: A blank with one or two words that each need a decision.
blueprints.harder: two words in the blank, both needing a decision (e.g. "the scientists' theories").

blueprints.title: Opening-phrase modifiers
blueprints.technique: The noun right after the comma must be who or what the opening phrase describes.
blueprints.build: An opening modifier, then a blank for the rest of the sentence.
wrong: passive voice that puts the wrong noun first
blueprints.harder: the opening phrase is long; two plausible actors.

blueprints.title: Transitions
blueprints.technique: Cover, Connect, Choose. Name the relationship (contrast, cause, addition, example, sequence), then pick from that group.
blueprints.build: Two or three sentences with a blank opening the last one.
wrong: one choice from each other relationship group
blueprints.harder: a sequence relationship; the relationship depends on the sentence two back. Never offer two same-meaning choices (therefore/thus) unless both are wrong.

blueprints.title: Notes / rhetorical synthesis
blueprints.technique: Read the goal first; turn it into a checklist (e.g. difference → names both things + contrast word + the named attribute).
blueprints.build: 'While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:' then 4–6 bullet notes on two related things, then 'The student wants to <goal>. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?'
wrong: true to the notes but the wrong attribute
only one of the two things
a similarity when a difference is asked (or the reverse)
blueprints.harder: goals like "introduce X to a new audience" or "present the findings".

blueprints.title: Main idea
blueprints.technique: Predict the main idea in your own words before reading choices; match the prediction.
blueprints.build: A short passage with a claim (often a "many assume… however…" turn). Some items ask for a stated detail instead ('According to the text…').
wrong: true but doesn't answer (an accurate detail, not the main idea)
half right (correct start, one wrong claim)
blueprints.harder: hedged language in the passage that makes 'too extreme' choices tempting; a literary passage.

blueprints.title: Textual evidence: support, weaken, illustrate
blueprints.technique: Restate the claim and split it into parts. The right answer matches every part. For weaken, it points the opposite way.
blueprints.build: A passage (40–100 words) stating one hypothesis with two parts, from an invented researcher. Quotation version: an original short poem or prose excerpt attributed to an invented author, and 'Which quotation from the poem most effectively illustrates the claim?'
wrong: supports when asked to weaken (or the reverse)
blueprints.harder: a weaken version; a quotation version.

blueprints.title: Quantitative evidence: tables
blueprints.technique: Read the claim first, then the title, labels and units. The right choice is true according to the data AND supports the claim.
blueprints.build: An invented study (40–100 words) plus a small Markdown table (2–4 rows × 2–4 columns) with a title line. Ask 'Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement/support the claim?'
wrong: true about the data but doesn't support the claim
supports the claim but misreads the data
about the wrong group or year
one number alone that doesn't show the change the claim needs
blueprints.harder: the claim compares two groups; the table has a distractor column.

blueprints.title: Inferences: most logically completes
blueprints.technique: Number the steps (what's established, what's ruled out, what's left) and predict before reading. The answer is the smallest statement the text forces.
blueprints.build: A 3–4 step chain of reasoning (60–120 words) ending in a blank: 'Which choice most logically completes the text?'
blueprints.harder: a negation in the chain; two premises that must be combined.

blueprints.title: Words in context
blueprints.technique: Cover the choices, find the clue (contrast, cause, restatement, example), predict your own word, then match meaning and tone.
blueprints.build: A passage (25–70 words) with one blank and a clear clue: 'Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?' Hard items may instead ask 'As used in the text, what does the word "X" most nearly mean?'
wrong: a word linked to the topic that doesn't fit the sentence
another meaning of a word with several meanings (hard)
blueprints.harder: the clue is a sentence away; a common word used in an unusual sense; sophisticated vocabulary at hard (e.g. tenuous, corroborate, idiosyncratic).

blueprints.title: Text structure and purpose
blueprints.technique: Ask why the text or sentence is there, not what it says. Describe its job with a verb (introduces, illustrates, challenges, qualifies) and check every part of the choice.
blueprints.build: A passage (50–120 words) with a clear structure: claim → example, view → counterpoint, problem → solution. Either 'Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?', '…main purpose of the text?', or '…function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?' (underline with <u>…</u>).
wrong: half right (right first verb, wrong second part)
the job of a different sentence
blueprints.harder: overall purpose of a passage with a turn; a 'qualifies' function; a literary passage.

blueprints.title: Cross-text connections
blueprints.technique: Summarize each text's claim in a few words, then name the relationship: agree, disagree, qualify, or add a new angle. Text 2's view is applied to Text 1's claim.
blueprints.build: Two short original texts labeled **Text 1** and **Text 2** (35–80 words each) on the same question. 'Based on the texts, how would <Text 2 author> most likely respond to <Text 1 claim>?'
blueprints.harder: a 'qualify' relationship; ask how Text 1's author would respond to Text 2.
